danishChanges.before: For det første, at en hustru sad adskilt fra sin mand i enkemanglens ensomhed, var ren ulykke — og ulykke, at høre, hvordan rygtets mange tunger alle forudsagde ondt — ulykke, når én kom og en anden fulgte efter, hver fortællende om frisk ulykke, jamrende gennem hal og kammer: »Tabt, tabt, alt tabt!« Havde denne min mand fået så mange sår, som rygtets tusind kanaler berettede, ville han have været mere fuld af huller end noget net. danishChanges.after: Først var det en lidelse at sidde skilt fra sin mand, ensom som en enke. Og en lidelse at høre rygtets mange tunger melde ulykke. Den ene kom efter den anden med stadig værre nyt og klagede gennem sale og kamre: _Tabt, tabt, alt er tabt!_ Havde min mand fået så mange sår, som rygtet ad tusind veje påstod, ville han have haft flere huller end et net. Var han blevet dræbt, hver gang der kom bud om hans død, kunne han nu kalde sig en ny Geryones med tre kroppe, dækket af tre lag jord — den jord, der ligger nedenunder, tæller jeg ikke — tre gange død, én død for hver krop. Så fortvivlet blev jeg over nyhederne om vrede og sorg, at jeg ofte lagde løkken om halsen for at dø, men andre rev den bort. Derfor står Orestes, dit og mit barn, tegnet og pantet på vores ægteskab, ikke her ved vores side, som han burde. Undr dig ikke. Han bor hos en trofast beskytter, Strofios, kongen af Fokis, som dengang advarede mig: _Tænk, dronning, hvilke ulykker der kan komme, og hvor uvist udfaldet er. Din mand er dagligt i fare ved Troja. Sov jeg, blev jeg vækket af den mindste lyd, selv en mygs summen, igen og igen fra urolige drømme, hvor jeg mærkede dig blive såret og så dig dræbt tre gange for hvert øjeblik, jeg sov.

englishChanges.before: See how through the wide city the swift feet of Rumor have run, roused by the joyful flame. But is the news they scatter true? Or do they perhaps offer for truth some deception that heaven has framed? A child he would be, and all unwise, who let his heart be stirred with joy at the rising of beacon-fires, only to sicken with deferred hope when some contrary word came. The edge of a woman's insight all too easily cuts good news off from true. Light rumors leap quickly within the bounds that fence in female credence — but the tale that springs from her guesswork, as lightly as it is born, dies just as lightly.

englishChanges.before: What remains is to think how best to honor and welcome my lord, the majesty of Argos, home again. What day shines fairer on a woman's eyes than this, on which she flings open the gate to greet her lord, shielded by heaven, returning from the war? Tell this to my husband — let him not delay, but come, and turn the city's longing into joy. Yes, let him come, and let him find when he comes a wife no different from the one he left: true and faithful as a watchdog to his home, foe to his foes, loyal in all her duties, trustworthy to keep for ten long years unbroken the store on which he set his master's seal. Steel must run deep with blood before you look to see ill joy or ill fame from any other man — least of all in me!

englishChanges.before: HERALD. It is true: Fate smiles at last. Throughout our hardship, all these years, some chances turned out fair, and some, I admit, were chequered with a curse. But who on earth has won the bliss of heaven, an unbroken prosperity through the whole length of his time? I could unfold a tale of toiling oars, of poor rest, of scant landings on rock-strewn shores — every kind of pain, every kind of sorrow, was our daily lot. And on land our woes were worse and more hateful, for where we slept, close beneath the enemy's wall, the river-plain was always damp with dews dropping from the sky and oozing from the earth — a curse that clung to our soaked clothing and to our hair, as bristling as a wild beast's hide. Why tell the woes of winter, when the birds lay stark and stiff, so cruel was the snow on Ida? Or summer's scorch, when the still wave sank to its sleep beneath the noonday sun? Why mourn old griefs? Their pain has passed; and for those who fell, all care has passed away forever — they will not rise again.
